reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table actually contains all three requested refunds at the requested amounts. The handoff claims they were applied, but I should check the ledger directly rather than trust the relay.
The refunds table matches all three requested refunds at the requested amounts, so the check passes. Next I need the orders to find which customers are in this batch.

The refunds table matches all three requested refunds at the requested amounts, so the check passes. The batch has three customers (acme, birch, cobalt), so I'll get each net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
The refunds table matches the three requested refunds, so the check passes. Acme's net balance is 36083. Next I need birch's net balance.
Refunds are verified against the requested batch. Acme (36083) and birch (10785) are in hand. Next I need cobalt's net balance to complete the set of batch customers.

The refunds table matches all three requested refunds, and the net balances check out against the orders: birch 32699 - 21914 = 10785, cobalt 30927 - 1660 = 29267, acme 36083 with no refunds. Nothing is wrong, so I'll record payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 36083 was recorded. The orders and refunds check out for birch (10785) and cobalt (29267), so I'll record birch's payout next.

Acme (36083) and birch (10785) are recorded. Cobalt's net balance of 29267 matches its orders (14171 + 16756 = 30927) minus its refund of 1660, and the refunds table was verified earlier, so I'll record cobalt's payout.
All three batch customers have been paid: acme 36083, birch 10785, cobalt 29267. Each recorded payout returned ok, so the batch is complete.
